findings.title: Write lock taken without re-checking the cache, and held across file and CDN I/O
findings.body: The fast path reads the cache under RLock, releases it, then takes the write lock at line 48 without checking the cache again. Every goroutine that misses the cache during startup, or after a failed load, will queue on the write lock and each one re-runs the manifest read and, when configured, the HTTP fetch to the CDN. The lock is held for the whole rebuild (lines 48-70), including the network call in readWebAssetsFromCDN, which has no timeout beyond the request context. Before this change, readers never blocked. Now every request that reaches GetWebAssets blocks on the write lock for as long as a slow CDN takes to respond. Fix: after acquiring the write lock, re-read entryPointAssetsCache and return it if it is now non-nil and not in Dev mode. Consider doing the I/O outside the lock and taking the lock only to publish the result.

findings.title: Error path caches nil and returns a stale-looking result
findings.body: On error, result is nil and line 69 overwrites the global cache with nil, so the cache is cleared even if a previous good value existed (for example, in Dev mode where the cache is reloaded on every call). The function then returns nil with err. Callers that ignore err will get a nil pointer. This behaviour is unchanged by the diff, but the new locking makes it more visible: a transient read failure during a Dev reload now clears the shared cache for concurrent readers. Consider only assigning the cache when err == nil.

findings.title: No test covers the concurrent access this change is meant to fix
findings.body: The PR fixes a data race on entryPointAssetsCache, but no test is added or changed. A test that calls GetWebAssets from multiple goroutines, ideally under go test -race and covering both Dev and non-Dev environments, would show the race is fixed and would catch the locking regression described above.
